questions.stem: A team of SQL developers needs a store for curated data that they will load and change with T-SQL, including multi-table transactions. Which Fabric item fits best?
questions.explanation: A Fabric warehouse gives full SQL transaction support, including multi-table transactions. A lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint is read-only for its tables, an eventhouse is built for KQL over event data, and a semantic model isn't a data store for engineering work.

questions.stem: Operations engineers need to query billions of timestamped device readings within seconds of their arrival, writing ad hoc queries in KQL. Which item fits best?
questions.explanation: An eventhouse holds KQL databases built for high-volume, time-based event data with near real-time ingestion and fast ad hoc queries.

questions.stem: Data engineers work in PySpark with a mix of JSON files, images and Delta tables, and want one store for files and tables. Which item fits best?
questions.explanation: A lakehouse stores files of any format alongside Delta tables and is designed for Spark. A warehouse holds relational tables for T-SQL work.

questions.stem: Which two statements about a lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint are true? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: It runs KQL queries over the lakehouse files
Its tables are read-only through T-SQL; you write them with Spark, pipelines or dataflows
It lets you query the lakehouse's Delta tables with T-SQL
It accepts INSERT and UPDATE statements on lakehouse tables
It needs its own capacity, separate from the lakehouse's

questions.explanation: Every lakehouse gets a SQL analytics endpoint for T-SQL queries over its Delta tables. You can create views and other objects there, but table data is written by the lakehouse's own tools, not by T-SQL DML.

questions.stem: An application team needs an operational store with high concurrency, full ACID transactions, enforced foreign keys and automatic performance tuning. Which Fabric item fits best?
questions.explanation: SQL database in Fabric is the choice for operational, transactional (OLTP) and normalized relational workloads. A warehouse is for analytics and BI, a lakehouse for big data and data engineering, and an eventhouse for streaming events.

questions.stem: A web app stores user profiles as JSON documents and needs a NoSQL database inside Fabric that developers reach through REST APIs from JavaScript and Python. Which item fits best?
questions.explanation: The decision guide maps NoSQL databases to Cosmos DB in Fabric, whose developers integrate through REST APIs. The other items are relational, event-analytics or Spark-based stores.

questions.stem: A team must store and model several terabytes of data. The data engineers work in notebooks, and the T-SQL users only query the data and never write INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE statements. Which item fits best?
questions.explanation: A lakehouse lets the engineers use Spark while T-SQL users consume the data through the SQL analytics endpoint. A warehouse suits a team that writes T-SQL and needs multi-table transactions, and the other two serve OLTP and streaming workloads.

questions.stem: Which Fabric data store doesn't make its data available in OneLake in open table format by default, so that you must opt in?

options.text: A KQL database in an eventhouse

questions.explanation: All Fabric data stores are in OneLake in open table format by default except a KQL database in an eventhouse, where OneLake availability is opt-in.

questions.stem: Report authors want to query a KQL database in an eventhouse through a SQL analytics endpoint, but the Analyze data with > SQL analytics endpoint option doesn't appear. What must be enabled on the database?

options.text: A materialized view for each table
A database shortcut to a lakehouse
Always-on and a minimum capacity schedule

questions.explanation: The SQL analytics endpoint option appears only when OneLake availability and schema synchronization are enabled. Always-on and minimum capacity affect performance, not SQL access.

questions.stem: A team wants to build an AI application that uses vector data types. Which two Fabric data stores does the decision guide recommend? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
questions.explanation: For AI development with vector data types, the guide names SQL database in Fabric or Cosmos DB in Fabric. Eventhouse, lakehouse and warehouse are recommended for other workloads.
